title: Level 4 Mastery: LLM Fundamentals & Prompting
description: Test your understanding of tokenization, context windows, few-shot prompting, and temperature controls.

questions.question: Roughly how many characters correspond to 1 token in typical English LLM tokenizers?
questions.explanation: As a general rule of thumb for English text, 1 token is approximately 4 characters or ~0.75 words.

questions.question: What happens when you set the LLM temperature parameter to 0.0?
options: The model produces the most deterministic, greedy outputs
The model doubles its inference latency
questions.explanation: Temperature = 0.0 makes the model select the highest probability token at each step (greedy decoding), maximizing consistency for agent tool calling.

questions.question: What is the core idea behind 'Chain-of-Thought' (CoT) prompting?
options: Connecting multiple LLMs in a blockchain ledger
Instructing the model to show intermediate reasoning steps before arriving at a final answer
Encoding the entire internet into a single prompt
Repeating the user query 10 times to boost model attention
questions.explanation: Encouraging the model to 'think step by step' allows it to allocate more reasoning tokens and significantly improves accuracy on complex multi-step tasks.

questions.question: Why is Few-Shot prompting effective for agent tool calling?
options: It provides concrete input-output demonstration pairs so the model learns the expected schema format
It fine-tunes the base model weights permanently on the server
It reduces token cost to zero
questions.explanation: In-context examples (few-shot) guide the model to follow specific output syntax and formatting constraints without retraining.
